title: Superpower #2: Align and Connect for Teamwork
coreMove: Draw the shared map before teams optimize locally and collide later.
sourcePressure: The second superpower introduces alignment and connection: visible priorities create shared direction and expose dependencies across teams.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Do not make alignment mean forced sameness or more communication meetings.

sourceAnchors.name: alignment and connection
sourceAnchors.detail: The source introduces alignment and teamwork as the second OKR superpower, stressing visible priorities and cross-team connection.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Alignment is the shared map; connection is the proof that teams can see how their work touches before collision happens.

hook: A team discovers OKRs in a conference room and suddenly gets aligned
A dashboard glows on a Monday morning and reveals the truth
A leader writes a goal on a whiteboard and everyone understands
opening with Superpower #2: Align and Connect for Teamwork as a definition rather than a pressure
counterintuition: Measurement is not bureaucracy, it is clarity
Goals are not dreams, they are systems
Accountability is not punishment, it is ownership
alignment is not a mindset, it is a system
tryThisNow: Set a timer and write three goals
Ask yourself what matters most right now
write one OKR without checking whether it changes behavior
examples: generic startup roadmap meeting with sticky notes
home chore chart with vague family goals
student group in a classroom choosing priorities
team lead reviewing a color-coded dashboard
